structured_output.world_model:
W3 (cost lens), after E019. The tip (E017 code) runs Muon with 3 Newton-Schulz steps and filters renormalized every step, so filter weight decay is inert. It also has Lookahead/EMA, resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps, batch 2000, widths 128/384/512, label smoothing 0.3, weight decay 0.006 on the SGD groups, 9.5 true epochs (HYP epochs=9.5, about 238 steps), and max-autotune with CUDA graphs. Measured: 6.548 s at 0.7537. E019 re-ran the same commit: 6.540 s at 0.7541. So the recipe, with the kernels selected now, sits at about 0.754 on seeds 0-2. E016's 0.7607 (math identical to E017 apart from the break removal) looks like a kernel or trajectory reshuffle, not true margin. My estimate of the true mean is about 0.755±0.002.

Time budget: time ≈ F + V × average pixel fraction.
- F is about 0.5-0.7 s, V about 7.8 s, and the average pixel fraction about 0.755.
- Systems levers are exhausted (E015, E017: host overhead under 1%).
- My time model has underpredicted savings twice (E011, E018). Lower-resolution steps save a bit more than pixel-proportional, perhaps because elementwise and memory traffic also shrink.
- Per-sample conv MACs: group 1 about 93M (its conv3 about 35M, about 7-8% of the total), group 2 about 240-280M (about 52%), group 3 about 129M.

Measured exchange rates (time per pp of accuracy):
- Last-group width: 1.6 s/pp (E010).
- Removing the 28 px phase: 1.6 s/pp (E018).
- Aggressive 20 px resizing: about 0.9 s/pp, but it was confounded (E011).
- Epochs: about 2 s/pp, noisy.
- Gains: Lookahead about +1 pp (E005); Muon +0.66 pp (E006); progressive resizing -22% time at about 0 pp (E007).
- Hyperparameter nudges (label smoothing, Muon lr, weight decay) all fall inside noise (E013, E014, E016/E017).

Every trim costs 1-2 s/pp, and the tip has about 0 pp of margin. Any pure trim of 3% or more therefore drops below 0.753 with high probability. The only path to a better feasible point is a near-free accuracy gain of at least 0.3 pp paired with a trim. None has been found. The remaining candidates are a BN-stat recompute after the EMA swap, a longer or plain EMA, a wider group 1 (cheap per pp?), and lower label smoothing at low resolution.

Mechanisms:
1. Endpoint averaging plus the fast-weight reset is worth about 1 pp (E005).
2. Accuracy is built across the mid- and high-resolution phases (E011, E018).
3. CIFAR-100 is width-hungry (E010).
4. Filter weight decay is inert (renormalization).
5. Kernel selection changes trajectories by up to about 0.7 pp at identical math (E016 vs E017/E019).

Noise:
- Per-seed std is about 0.3 pp, so the 3-seed standard error is about 0.17 pp.
- Rebuild shifts can be larger.
- Time noise is about 0.5-1%.

Unsure:
- The 40-seed mean on the PCIe judge, likely 0.754-0.756, which is marginal for 0.75 but fine.
- Whether any accuracy lever beats noise.
- How efficient tensor cores are at width 320.

forecasts.reason: The cut is 25 steps, about 10% of time. At about 2 s/pp that costs about 0.4-0.6 pp from a 0.754 base, so the run falls below the bar and below the hypothesis's 0.7545 floor.
The cut removes about 13% of MACs, so time drops by about 7%. CIFAR-100 is width-hungry, so the loss should be about 0.4 pp, and the hypothesis allows at most 0.25 pp against E016.
Weight-decay nudges have been noise. The hypothesis needs +0.2 pp over E016's 0.7607, which was itself an outlier.
Group 1's conv3 is only about 8% of MACs plus some elementwise traffic, so the time cut is about 6%, short of the 8% target. Losing depth at high resolution should cost about 0.3 pp.
Only the first 15% of steps move from 24 to 20 px. That saves about 0.2-0.25 s (about 3.5%, under the 4% target) and loses about 0.15 pp, which puts the run at the bar.

cruxes: What did E019's held-out seeds 3-12 give for the 10-seed mean? If it is at least 0.757, there is about 0.3 pp of real margin to spend on one trim, such as I035 or a 0.5-epoch cut. If it is about 0.754, every trim fails.
Is there any time-neutral accuracy lever worth at least 0.3 pp, such as a BN-stat recompute after the EMA swap, a plain EMA, or a wider group 1 at low resolution? That would fund a 1-2 s/pp trim.
Does a rebuild deterministically reselect the same kernels? E016 vs E017/E019 suggests about 0.7 pp of rebuild noise, which would make all 3-seed keep decisions unreliable at this margin.
